rows.label: sphere-centred, every line in a TRUE GOLD hue (~75) — the gold the palette does not declare
rows.framingWhy: the ink bounding box of the whole figure — the sphere fills the tab
rows.byrne: Byrne's yellow is the one ink row C could not use here (round 21 solved that window); this row asks the same question at tab size instead of hero size
rows.reading: the honest price of a gold LINE, measured: on PAPER the solve lands at L 55 (`oklch(55% 0.14 75)` = `#a06200`, 4.59 against paper), which the record flags as BELOW the L 60 floor at which a hue ~75 colour reads as gold — a bronze line that satisfies the arithmetic and the eye separately. On INK it lands at L 60 (`#b07100`, 4.59 against ink) and that one reads as gold. So the same hue is a gold on the dark tab and a bronze on the light one, and the reason is the bar, not the hue. Either way the row costs a token @theme does not have: `check:favicon` refuses `#a06200` and `#b07100` with "is not a token (nearest: --color-accent renders #a2432a)", and the candidate names are printed as candidates, not as tokens. At 16px the row is also QUIETER than the ratified pair it replaces — T1 measures 87 any / 61 at3 px, this row 90 any / 62 at3 but a max contrast of 4.59 against 17.15 — so a gold line buys prominence in HUE and pays for it in CONTRAST.

rows.label: the full 240x150 plate, and the PLATE ITSELF is the gold
rows.framingWhy: the drawing exactly as the hero draws it, non-square
rows.byrne: 1847 printing shows a diagram on a tinted plate: the colour is the surface the figure sits on, which is the one place a gold has room in this palette (the LAYER bar is 1.35, not 4.5)
rows.reading: the gold with the most area — and the price that corrects a guess: a gold GROUND is not judged by the 1.35 layer bar, it is judged by the gate's 4.5 PAIR bar against the lines drawn over it, so the solve lands at L 60 under `ink` lines (`#b07100`, 4.59, reads as gold) and at L 55 under `paper` lines (`#a06200`, 4.59, BELOW the gold-ness floor). Gold on the light page, bronze on the dark one — the mirror image of the gold-line row, because the plate swaps which colour it is measured against. It is also the row that changes what the tab's ground MEANS: a gold plate is the site's colour replacing the browser's own background, and the 96 blank px a 240x150 plate leaves in a 16px slot (37.5% of the tab, measured) become gold bands. Costs a token @theme does not have.
